chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man divorces his wife while he is absent, and he knows that on the day he divorced her, she was menstruating. He said: 'It is valid.'
And validity of the divorce of the absent man is required in all cases if his absence is a month or more, and what indicates that is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if the husband is absent and knows his wife is menstruating?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the validity of a divorce pronounced by an absent husband is confirmed even if he knows his wife is menstruating, a scenario often debated regarding the 'period of purity' (Taharah) requirement. The text further clarifies that for such a divorce to be universally valid regardless of specific conditions, the husband's absence must be at least one month, a ruling supported by additional narrations. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the objective status of the wife's purity cycle rather than the husband's immediate presence or knowledge.
